> **Maintainer:** adapt this file to the project, then run `python3 tools/lb.py protect` and
> commit. It is write-protected for the assistant: conventions are set by the human.

The conventions below bind every entry. An entry that deviates from one says so explicitly.

## Identifiers and labels

- Entries: `YYYY-MM-DD_slug`; runs: `R-NNNN`; events: `E-NNNN`.
- Quarto labels carry the entry slug as prefix: `fig-<slug>-<name>`, `eq-<slug>-<name>`,
  `tbl-<slug>-<name>`; cross-references with `@fig-<slug>-<name>`.

## Numbers

- Numbers in the text come from the ledger via shortcodes (`{{</* result R-0007 metric */>}}`,
  `{{</* run-param R-0007 key */>}}`); a number typed by hand names its source.
- Every quantity carries its unit.

## Abbreviations and run names

- Every entry, summary and audit defines each abbreviation it uses, in the document itself, in its
  section "Abbreviations": run names (`BASE`, `FP1`, ...), configuration or template tags, decision
  labels, defect and audit labels, and field-specific shorthands. One line each: what it is, what
  makes it different (parameters, code version, machine), and where it is defined in full.
- Abbreviations defined in another entry are defined again, briefly. A reader of one entry must not
  need a second one to understand it.
- Compact notations for points of the parameter space (tuples, grid indices) are spelled out with
  their quantities and units at first use.
